QF.id: SIA Case Studies on SAS Standards_15

question.text: For a SAS-200 sanitation programme delivering toilets to 6,875 households (AB Responsible Services context), the Means of Verification (MoV) for the OUTCOME 'reduction in open defecation' is BEST triangulated through:

answer.text: Photographs of toilets at construction time only

Triangulation of (i) physical inspection of functional toilets, (ii) beneficiary self-report, (iii) village-level Swachh Bharat database check, (iv) school-attendance data (especially girls) as indirect outcome indicator
The SE Managing Director's written confirmation

explanation.text: **The Logic:** A robust MoV design triangulates construction output (physical inspection), self-report (survey), administrative data (SBM database) and a behavioural proxy (school attendance). Single-source data is insufficient under SAS-200 — exactly how the case studies structure evidence. **The Trap:** Options A, B and D rely on single-source evidence — each has a known weakness (photos prove output not outcome; self-report has social desirability bias; MD letter is management representation). **Cross-Exam Context:** Triangulation matches the audit-evidence sufficiency logic in III-A / III-C (Compliance) and the 'Use of multiple sources' principle in XV (Research Analyst). **Assessor's Pro-Tip:** Draft a one-page MoV matrix per indicator: four columns = 4 independent sources, one row per indicator. If fewer than 2 sources tick for an indicator, escalate or drop the indicator.
